aperture_validity.basis: The source states no aperture stop; the beam is limited by the element clear apertures.
aperture_validity.satisfaction_basis: No field-dependent measurement or pupil sample is recorded, so a stop-dependent match is not claimed.
aperture_validity.consequence: A stop-dependent constraint stays unconfirmed for this record.

spectrum.sampling_wavelengths_basis: The publication states its reference wavelength in air at 20 C and 101325 Pa; it is converted once with the engine's own air model (material_physics.air_index_exact) to the vacuum wavelength the engine evaluates.
spectrum.wavelength_precision: The converted value is a computational value at full precision; a reviewer may pass it to the engine unchanged. Rounding in prose is for display only.

continuous_coverage_nm.note: The publication states a single reference wavelength, not a specified band.

effective_focal_length_mm.definition: Effective focal length as printed for the example
effective_focal_length_mm.conditions: Reference wavelength; the stated object distance.

back_focal_length_mm.definition: Paraxial distance from the exit vertex to the rear focal point, positive downstream

total_track_mm.definition: First surface vertex to the exit vertex along the axis, from the committed Project

engine_check.method: Thick-lens ABCD through the committed Project at the reference wavelength.

comparison.rule: |engine - source| <= atol + rtol * |source|. atol covers the printed focal length; rtol covers the prescription printed to three or four decimals in radius, thickness and index together with the engine's air-referenced index convention.

magnification.basis: The publication prints no magnification, or the output is collimated and a magnification needs a tube lens that this record does not carry.

object_numerical_aperture.definition: Object-side numerical aperture derived from the printed entrance aperture 53.5 mm and the printed focal length 80 mm (NA = D/(2 f)); the publication prints an aperture ratio of 1:1.23, not an NA

working_distance_mm.definition: Object distance to the first surface minus the stated cover-glass thickness

object_distance_mm.definition: Distance from the object plane to the first surface vertex, the value the prescription tabulates

field.definition: Largest object-space field height the publication states
field.note: The publication states no object field, so the field constraint is unconfirmed.

materials.basis: Each glass is modelled from the printed nd and Abbe number: a two-term Cauchy curve through (nd, Vd) is fitted by a three-term Sellmeier with fixed poles over 450-660 nm.

model_glasses.basis: ND_VD_CAUCHY_SELLMEIER fit to the printed nd=1.53019 and Vd=67.58
ND_VD_CAUCHY_SELLMEIER fit to the printed nd=1.75844 and Vd=52.1
ND_VD_CAUCHY_SELLMEIER fit to the printed nd=1.48794 and Vd=80.07

ND_VD_CAUCHY_SELLMEIER fit to the printed nd=1.62286 and Vd=60.08

approximations.description: The publication states nd and Vd only. A two-term Cauchy curve is solved exactly from those two values and a three-term Sellmeier with fixed poles is fitted to it over the stated band. The index at the reference wavelength is the source's nd; the dispersion curve is a model.
The Project's environment is air, so the engine reports first-order quantities relative to the air index at the reference wavelength; the source's own focal length is a design value.

The publication states no clear apertures. Each semi-diameter is the height of the real meridional marginal ray at the stated object-side NA with a mechanical allowance, reduced where an element edge or an air gap would otherwise be impossible. They are estimates, not the source's own apertures.
The design is corrected for an infinite image distance, so the Project places the observation plane at a finite standoff instead of at a focal point; no image-side quantity is claimed.
